paragraphs.source_en: Even before the failure of the rescue mission, some of the President’s advisers had felt there was a need to act decisively so as not to look impotent. “We need to do something,” Zbigniew Brzezinski—the President’s National Security Advisor—said, “to reassure the Egyptians, the Saudis and others on the Arabian peninsula that the US is prepared to assert its power.” And that meant establishing “a visible military presence in the area now.”67 — The United States was not alone, however, in trying to find a response to the tumultuous events that would enable it to protect its interests and reputation. On 22 September, Iraq began a surprise attack on Iran, bombing Iranian airfields and launching a three-pronged ground invasion that targeted the province of Khūzestān and the cities of Ābādān and Khurramshahr. There were no doubts in Iranian minds about who lay behind these attacks.
